paragraphs: CENTEGIX sells emergency alerting for schools, built around a solution called CrisisAlert that lets any staff member call for help. The alert carries the exact floor, room or hallway rather than just a building name.

When a full alert fires, strobes and intercoms activate across the campus. Arriving responders are shown the precise location of the person who pressed the button. The company is careful to say that most of what it handles is not an active shooter but a medical emergency, a behavioral crisis or a student leaving campus. Around the alerting sit other modules, including visitor management for authenticating and locating people on campus. Reunification is handled the same way, with a guardian verified before any student is handed over. Rollout starts with a short discovery call that maps buildings and looks for gaps in response.

School districts are the core audience, with the product framed as giving staff the confidence to act quickly. The same technology is offered to healthcare organizations facing workplace violence. A third line is aimed at public servants and the staff who work alongside them. The company says the product was built by former educators, law enforcement officers and caregivers. It also convenes an invitation-only customer advisory board drawn from senior safety leaders.

quote.text: CENTEGIX was founded on the idea that technology can create safer, more secure environments.
